_note_daily_overhead_day_model: days = setup + rate x SQ, least-squares fit over Tim's 30-home TIME LEARNING log (docs/ROOFR_OVERHEAD_TIERS.md). Tile R2 0.70 / Metal 0.66 fit well; demo+shingle are noisy (R2 ~0.37) — refit when Tim logs tear-off type. Low-slope systems are deliberately absent: no fitted data, so their labor days stay manual.

daily_overhead_day_model._note_geometry_model: days = intercept + coef*feature over RoofR cut measurements, fitted per series on Tim's 30-home log with NON-NEGATIVE coefficients (scripts/fit_days_from_roofr.py). Preferred over the squares-only fit above whenever a quote carries cut LFs, because Tim's method is time-driven and time tracks complexity, not area (Zoom 2026-07-17 [10:12]). Leave-one-out R2 in loo_r2. Negative coefficients are eliminated on purpose: 'more valleys means fewer days' is noise, and it under-prices the complex roofs that actually take longer.

pitch_day_adder._note: Steep-roof day adder. Tim books more time than the geometry model predicts on steep roofs: measured residual -0.29 days at <=4/12, +0.03 at 5/12, +0.64 at >=6/12 across his 29 homes. Applied to the INSTALL series only, once per job. A threshold rule rather than a fitted coefficient because only 7 of the 29 homes are >=6/12 and pitch as a regressor made every install series worse out-of-sample. NO homes in the sample are >=7/12, where Tim's own sheet says cost jumps ($305/sq tile adder) — revisit when he labels steeper roofs.

low_slope._note_insulation_by_thickness: Tim's sheet K15/K16/K17: 1" board ($50 L, $155 M, $50 OH) = $255; 1.5" ($50/$175/$50) = $275; 2" ($50/$210/$50) = $310. Per-sq, no profit. These are keyed on BOARD THICKNESS, not job size. The old insulation_tiers schema was [max_sq, price]; because thickness is not size every row carried max_sq:null, so the lookup returned on the first row and EVERY low-slope job priced at the 1" rate. Superseded 2026-07-25; insulation_tiers is retained only so already-seeded configs keep resolving via the positional fallback in low_slope_insulation_cost().
